title: An Overbooked Calendar Isnt a Strategy
author: Honest Office
summary: Our culture has made meeting attendance a badge of honor and a proxy for importance, yet research shows meetings are the number one barrier to productivity. Back-to-back meetings cause cognitive recovery deficits; people need transition time between social interaction. Shopify deleted all recurring meetings with 3+ people and blocked meeting-free work time. Makers (writers, programmers, teachers) need half-day blocks; managers work in hourly intervals. Creating calendar relief is essential for deep, generative work.
points: Meetings are considered ineffective 72% of the time and are the top barrier to productivity.
Back-to-back meetings cause neurological recovery deficits; the brain needs transition time.
Makers require half-day blocks to do quality work; hour-long intervals are barely enough to get started.
Meeting culture has become a badge of honor disconnected from actual impact or output.
Organizations like Shopify saw gains by deleting recurring meetings and protecting meeting-free work blocks.
quotes: An overbooked calendar isn't a strategy, but a calendar with ample time and space for deep work certainly is.
Meetings aren't just considered ineffective 72% of the time, but also deemed the number one barrier to productivity.
You can't write or program well in units of an hour. That's barely enough time to get started.
A packed calendar dictates our sense of worth and accomplishment, even if the meetings aren't producing much.
The importance of providing calendar relief at a systemic level becomes all the more important.” Archived from Honest Office on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
